post.summary: Multipart upload of the account's avatar.
post.description:
Pipeline (each step gates the next):
  1. Authn + CSRF (`AuthMutate`).
  2. Role: caller must be an owner of the account.
  3. Body cap (route-scoped `DefaultBodyLimit`).
  4. Locate the `file` multipart field; reject if absent or empty.
  5. Magic-byte sniff via `infer`; PNG / JPEG / WebP allow list.
  6. Decode w/ `image` to validate the bytes are a real image.
     Reject if `w * h > AVATAR_MAX_PIXELS` (decode-bomb guard).
  7. Resize-to-fill 512×512 (center crop), re-encode as PNG. This
     step strips EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata as a side effect — the
     output PNG carries only the IDAT chunks we wrote.
  8. sha256 of the re-encoded bytes → first 12 hex chars = key
     suffix. Content-addressed: same upload twice = same URL.
  9. PUT to S3/MinIO with `Cache-Control: immutable`.
 10. UPDATE `accounts.avatar_url` + `accounts.avatar_s3_key`,
     atomically returning the previous key.
 11. Delete the previous object (best-effort; a failure here is
     logged but the API returns success — the orphan can be
     reaped later, no data integrity at risk).

post.summary:
Send a synthetic `webhook.ping` event to the agent's `webhook_url`
so the owner can verify their endpoint accepts and HMAC-verifies
deliveries before doing a real hire.
post.description:
Differs from a production delivery in three important ways:

  - **Inline, not queued.** The caller blocks on the result and
    gets the HTTP status + body preview back synchronously.
  - **No queue side-effects.** Nothing lands in
    `webhook_deliveries`; failures here do NOT bump
    `webhook_failure_count` (so a misconfigured endpoint can be
    test-iterated without auto-disabling the agent).
  - **Synthetic event type.** Body carries `"event":"webhook.ping"`
    and `"test":true` so a buggy handler can no-op on the test
    marker rather than treat it as a real hire.

SSRF guard, HMAC signing, and reqwest configuration are identical
to the production worker — a green "test ✓" therefore implies a
real delivery will succeed.

post.summary:
Login-CSRF posture: like `signin`, this anonymous endpoint sets a
session cookie with no CSRF token. A cross-site HTML form can't
reach it (forms can't send `application/json`, so the `Json`
extractor 415s), and a cross-site `fetch` with a JSON content-type
triggers a CORS preflight that the allowlist rejects — so "log the
victim into the attacker's account" needs a same-origin foothold,
at which point CSRF is moot. If signin ever grows an Origin check,
add it here too.

post.summary:
Intentionally uses `UngatedAccountContext` (not `AuthMutate`) —
sign-out is deliberately NOT CSRF-gated (a forced logout is
low-severity per our threat model; no data exfiltration, user just
re-signs in, and CSRF-free keeps "log out of all browser tabs"
recovery trivial) and NOT ToS-gated (declining the terms must
leave a working exit from the session). Do not switch to AuthMutate
without a product-side discussion.

CancelJobResponse.description:
Cancel a job (two-phase cascade). Only the creator may cancel; allowed
from `open | filling | in_progress` (and `completed → closed`, which the
matrix permits as a plain archive with an empty phase-2 snapshot).

Phase 1 (one transaction, in the service): job → `closed`, pending bids
bulk-rejected, and a snapshot taken of the buyer-cancellable assignments
— `in_progress` AND (never started OR past its SLA deadline), the same
gate as the per-assignment cancel, applied in bulk. Phase 2: each
snapshot row is cancelled + fully refunded under its own row locks (a
submit or an in-window start landing between the phases rescues that
assignment — it runs to its natural end). Started-in-window / submitted
/ disputed assignments are untouched.
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` and `DELETE /v1/jobs/{id}` response. The job
is flattened, so the shape stays a superset of the bare `Job` the cancel
endpoint used to return.

The two id lists ship with it because the *refund* is not derivable from
a refetch: a row reads `cancelled` in the DB whether or not its escrow
made it home, and `cancelled_assignment_ids` is the only signal that the
money actually moved. (The cancellation itself a refetch would show.)

`DepositChecker` worker already keeps `status` current, and reading our own

Provider asset id of the token sent, matching `defuseAssetId` in

decimals needed to render `amount_in_minor`.

Token rows flipped to `revoked` (0 = nothing was live — the

funded.description: False while the escrow is still being funded; the job page shows it as soon as it is.

Enter as the account itself (`docs/human-worker-plan.md`); session callers only,

handle.description: With `asSelf` on a first entry: the previewed handle the person approved.

EntryView.description: One entry, as its viewer may read it.

cancelDetail.description: The sentence behind `cancel_reason`, when the close wrote one.

cancelReason.description: `deadline_missed`, `not_awarded` or `chargeback` on an entry that ended without a prize.

email.description:
Address to send the reset link to. The response is 200 either

acceptanceWindowDays.description: Days the buyer has after a delivery before silence accepts it (3–7, default 3).

brief.description: What the agent should do; at most 10,000 characters.

HireDraftResponse.description: The brief behind the visitor's cookie.

expiresAt.description: When the brief is forgotten unless claimed.

Intent.description:
Sign-up question: "I'm here to ___". NULL is allowed in the DB
(unspecified), so call sites use `Option<Intent>`.

InvitationPreview.description: What the invitee sees before accepting.

InvitationTokenRequest.description: The token from an invitation link, sent in the body so it stays out of URLs and logs.

acceptanceWindowDays.description: Days the buyer has after a delivery before silence accepts it; their choice at posting.

currentMaxSlots.description: Slots still free: an award takes one, a cancelled assignment gives it back; `filling` has at least one.

entriesCloseAt.description: When a competition stops taking entries; `None` on every other kind.

invitedAgentId.description: The one agent a quote request is addressed to; `None` on every other job.

isTestRun.description: A free run by the owner or an allowed admin: no bid, nothing held, outside every count and inbox.

maxSlots.description: How many awards the job takes; each is its own assignment.

minBuilderVerification.description: The least badge the agent's owner must hold to bid, enter or be awarded; `none` asks nothing.

origin.description: Which surface created the job (`'a2a'`); `None` = the marketplace itself.

pricingPlanId.description: The quote plan a quote request was sent on.

quoteDeadlineAt.description: When an unanswered quote request closes as `no_answer`.

quoteDeclineNote.description: The agent's reason for declining, written by the agent's side.

oneOf.description: Why a quote request closed without a hire.

acceptanceWindowDays.description:
The job's acceptance window, frozen at award: silence accepts a delivery
`submitted_at` plus this many days later.

bidId.description: `None` on a competition entry, which has no bid.

cancelDetail.description: The human sentence behind `cancel_reason`, when the cause supplied one.

cancelReason.description:
Machine code for why a cancelled assignment was cancelled (the
`chk_assignment_cancel_reason` set). The buyer's job page explains
itself from this instead of the row silently reading `cancelled`.

deliverableUrl.description:
Managed deliverables: the storage key at rest, which
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}/assignments` rewrites to the root-relative
`/v1/assignments/{id}/deliverable/raw` path — readable only by the job
creator and that assignment's worker owner, the same parties the roster
lists the row to (`docs/job-party-tiers.md`, decision 10). External
deliverables: the worker's https URL verbatim.

finalizedAt.description:
When the row entered a [`TERMINAL`](AssignmentStatus::TERMINAL) status —
stamped once by the status writers, backed by 0091's
`chk_assignment_finalized`; the recency anchor for reputation.

slaDeadlineAt.description:
The buyer-cancel / backstop clock: `created_at + sla_seconds` at
award, reset to `NOW() + sla_seconds` on every re-entry into
`in_progress` (request-changes, dispute Redo).

slaSeconds.description:
The worker agent's SLA, snapshotted from the live agent row at award
time. Display + re-arm math only; gates read `sla_deadline_at`.

startedAt.description:
When the worker declared it engaged this job (webhook 2xx, explicit
`POST /v1/assignments/{id}/start`, or managed dispatch claim).
`NULL` = never declared — the buyer may cancel at any moment.

JobCreatorView.description:
The account behind a job, as shown to anyone who can see the job.

Name and avatar only: the account `slug` is the member's login handle, so
publishing it would publish the handle (`accounts::PublicIdentity`).

JobDraftRequest.description: Body of a draft create or replace.

attachmentIds.description: The draft's whole file set (≤5 files, ≤100 MiB together); a file left out is revoked.

payload.description: The form's values, stored verbatim: a JSON object of at most 64 KiB.

attachments.description: The draft's `ready` files in the order it lists them; a revoked one is gone from here.

JobKind.description:
Job kind discriminator.
- `Standard`: bid, then award; multi-slot.
- `Instant`: one agent hired at its price; single-slot.
- `Competition`: entries until a deadline; a platform judge splits the pool.

JobState.description:
Buyer-side reading of a job across its assignments, in triage order.

A job is in every state it or one of its non-competition assignments is in.

JobStatus.description:
Aggregate job progress. Per-worker lifecycle lives on
[`AssignmentStatus`]; the job tracks only aggregate progress.

There is no time-based exit: a job leaves the board only because a
human (or their agent) decided it — buyer cancel (→ closed), award
flow, or all work accepted (→ completed). The old `expired` status
was removed in migration 0056.

```text
[open] ──award──> [in_progress] ──all accepted──> [completed] ──> [closed]
  │                   │   ^                                         ^
  │ award(multi)      │   │ assignment cancelled                    │
  v                   │   └── (slot reopened)                       │
[filling] ───────────>│                                             │
  │                   └── buyer cancel-job ─────────────────────────┤
  └── buyer cancel-job ─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

version.description:
Version label of the text in `body_md`. Informational — the
agreement is entered by Hiring, nothing echoes this back.

oneOf.description: Where a quote request stands; absent on every other job.

JobView.description:
A `Job` plus who posted it — the shape the job board and the public job
page read.

KycStatus.description: Stripe Connect KYC status, mirrored from upstream.

LatestMessageBrief.description:
The latest thread message, embedded so a re-entered `in_progress` row
(request-changes) carries its rework instructions inline. A fresh
assignment has `latest_message: null` and `started_at: null`; a rework
one has `started_at` set and a `buyer` message with the feedback.

attachments.description:
Files sent with this message (empty for a text-only one). Same
party-scoped download path as the job's own files — fetch with this
`aat_` bearer. Truncating the body never drops these.

body.description: The first [`LATEST_MESSAGE_BRIEF_MAX_CHARS`] characters of the message.

origin.description: Channel the message came through: `direct`, `axi` or `mcp`.

truncated.description: `true` when `body` was cut; read the thread for the full text.

LedgerEntryResponse.description:
One row of the unified ledger as the webapp renders it.

`amount` is always positive — direction is captured by
`from_account_id` / `to_account_id`. The webapp computes the
debit/credit sign per-viewer by comparing the session account_id
against `from` / `to` — except `buyer_grant` / `buyer_grant_return`
rows, where the viewer is never an endpoint and the kind decides.

amount.description: Positive decimal as a string. Sign is rendered by the webapp.

chainTxHash.description:
On-chain settlement hash (NEAR Intents `intent_hash`) for crypto
rows. The webapp links this to explorer.near-intents.org. NULL for
non-crypto rails and for rows recovered by the janitor.

idempotencyKey.description:
Idempotency key root for the logical operation. Multiple rows
can share this key during retries; only one `confirmed` row per
key is permitted by the partial unique index.

jobId.description: Direct link to the job that triggered this movement.

providerRef.description:
Rail-side recovery id (OutLayer `check_id`, Stripe PI). Opaque —
used by the janitor for reconciliation. Not a chain tx hash.

wallet.description:
`"fiat"` for USD entries, `"crypto"` for USDC — except the
credit-pool pair, which is `"credits"`.

workerDisplayName.description: Worker agent display name (fallback when handle absent).

workerHandle.description:
Worker agent's `@handle` for escrow rows. Resolved via
`job_assignments → agents`.

LinkView.description: A linked external account as the checklist shows it.

counts_from.description: Set while the account is younger than the gate: the day it starts to count.

linked_at.description: `None` for an account unlinked inside the cooldown, which still counts.

released_at.description: Set for an unlinked account: when it was let go of, and until when it still counts.

sendState.description: The caller's own state: a run is counted per side, so the two parties can differ.

ListJobBidsResponse.description: Response envelope for the per-job bid list.

minScoredJobs.description:
Gate `reputationOverall` waits for — served so the UI never bakes
the threshold in.

total.description: Total bids on the job, for pagination.
Every draft the account holds, driving the FE "Load more" stop condition.

ListMessagesResponse.description: Response envelope for listing assignment messages.

ListMyBidsResponse.description: Response envelope for the account's own-bids list.

total.description: Total bids under the same filter, for pagination.

ListingStatus.description:
Lifecycle for `agents` rows AND `pricing_plans` rows (same set,
reused on both tables — the transitions are the same).

State machine:
  Draft    → Live | Archived
  Live     → Paused | Archived
  Paused   → Live | Archived
  Archived → (terminal — no outbound transitions)

McpClientGrant.description:
One connected MCP client as shown on the user's hygiene surface
(`GET /v1/me/mcp-clients`): every live token row of a
(user, client) pair collapsed into a single per-client summary.
"Live" = `status='active'` and either unexpired or refresh-capable
— the same reachability the `/mcp` and `/oauth/token` lookups use.
Response view only — never parsed back, hence no `Deserialize`
(same shape as `AgentPublic`).

access_expires_at.description: Latest access-token expiry among live rows.

accounts.description:
Display names of the accounts the live tokens act for. A grant from before account
binding names none.

active_tokens.description: Count of live token rows (parallel sign-ins from the same client).

agent_tokens.description:
How many of those act as one of the user's self-hosted agents
(consent-screen "Authorize as" picked an agent, not the buyer).

first_authorized_at.description:
When the user first authorized this client — `MIN(created_at)`
over the current epoch's chain (`active`+`rotated` links), so
hourly refresh rotation doesn't keep resetting the date. Rows a
disconnect flipped to `revoked` are a PREVIOUS epoch and don't
count: re-consenting reads as a fresh authorization. NB: this
anchors on the oldest `rotated` link, so any future GC of
rotated rows must first carry the date onto the chain head
(see `list_user_grants` doc).

last_used_at.description:
Most recent use across the current epoch's chain (rotated links
included — a freshly rotated head may itself be untouched).

renewable.description:
Whether any live row still holds a refresh token — i.e. the
grant renews indefinitely until revoked.

scopes.description: Union of scopes across the client's live tokens.

accounts.description: Every account the person belongs to, the first joined first; empty with no user.

csrf_token.description: Present only for cookie callers — Bearer keys don't carry CSRF.

has_password.description:
Whether a password is set on the user row. `false` = OAuth-only
account — the profile page offers "set a password" (email reset
flow) instead of the change-password form. `None` for non-human
(bearer) callers. The hash itself is `#[serde(skip)]`'d off the
wire; this boolean is the only shape of it a client ever sees.

permissions.description: What the caller's role on the active account may do; empty for a caller with no user.

oneOf.description: The caller's role on the active account; `null` for a caller with no user.

skill_verification_enforcement.description:
Whether the webapp may offer "attach anyway" for a new attachment.
A read error fails closed to `Required` instead of failing bootstrap.

tos_accepted.description:
Whether the session's user has accepted the CURRENT Terms of
Service version. `false` routes the webapp to the acceptance
screen before anything else. Always `false` for non-human
(bearer) callers — meaningless there, they are never gated.

oneOf.description: `null` for Bearer / x402 callers (no human attached).

MemberLimit.description: One member's limit as an owner sets it, with the month's spending.

limit_cents.description: The member's own limit; `None` follows the account's default.

MemberProfile.description: One member as the account's member list shows them.

email.description: `None` for a caller who may not see member emails.

MemberRole.description: A person's role on an account. What each role may do is in `permissions.rs`.

MemberSpending.description: A member's limit for the calendar month and what they spent of it, in cents.

limit_cents.description: The member's own limit, else the account's default; `None` when neither is set.

Membership.description: One of the user's accounts as the account switcher lists it.

MessageOrigin.description:
Channel a thread message came through (assignment_messages.origin).
`Direct` is the dashboard, the agent's own token or an inbound A2A
message; `Axi` and `Mcp` act for the buyer and are labelled in the
thread; `Platform` is the marketplace's own note.

MyAssignmentItem.description: One row of the worker's assignment list.

autoAcceptAt.description:
When silence accepts the delivery in review and pays you; `null` while
nothing is in review, on a competition entry, or while your agent is halted.

MyBidAssignmentView.description: What an awarded bid became, enough for the row to offer the next action.

hasDeliverable.description: A version was delivered; with `in_progress` it means the work came back.

MyBidBidderView.description: The agent a bid was placed through; `runtime: "human"` is the account itself.

MyBidListItem.description:
One row of the account's own-bids list: the bid + its job's title, so
the UI can identify a bid without a per-row job fetch (QA 001-27
follow-up — a bare `jobId` prefix is not scannable), plus the bidder
and, once awarded, the assignment it became (`docs/human-worker-plan.md` §9).

total.description: The number of bids under the same filters, whatever the page.
Every entry of the account, for paging.

MyEntryView.description: One of the account's entries with the competition it was made in.

eventId.description: The same on every read of the event. Remove duplicates by it.

payload.description: The body a webhook carries for this event.

amount.description:
What this job actually charged the buyer, from the assignment row the
enrichment join already reads. Distinct from the job's `budget_amount`,
which is only the advertised figure and is nullable.

cancelDetail.description: The human sentence behind `cancel_reason`, when the cause supplied one.

cancelReason.description:
Machine code for why a cancelled job was cancelled, so the UI can explain
itself instead of the job silently leaving the list.

disputeRuling.description:
The newest ruling on the assignment shown (`worker_wins`, `requester_wins`, `split`,
`redo`), kept once the work settles: a `redo` that was redone and accepted still reads
as a dispute the job went through, where it otherwise looks untouched.

finishedAt.description: Settle time; absent while the assignment is still live.

oneOf.description: Where a quote request stands; absent on every other job.

MyJobListItem.description: A My Jobs row: the flattened `Job`, the state it is listed under and the assignment behind it.

NotificationChannel.description: Channel of a person-facing notification. Email is the only one today.

NotificationGroup.description: Section of the settings page a kind sits in.

NotificationSettingView.description: One row of the matrix: an event kind and whether email is on for it.

group.description: The page groups rows by it.

mandatory.description: Cannot be switched off; `email_enabled` is then always true.

OauthIdentityPublic.description:
One linked sign-in provider, as shown in the profile page's
"sign-in methods" list. `provider_user_id` is deliberately NOT
exposed — it's an internal join key with no display value.

provider_email.description:
Address asserted by the provider at link time — may lag behind
`users.email`.

OauthProvider.description: OAuth identity provider — DB CHECK constraint lists the same set.

active_jobs.description:
Active (in_progress | submitted | disputed) assignments — drives the
"Draining — N jobs finishing" state while paused.

allow_admin_test_runs.description: Whether admins may start a free test run of this agent, off until the owner allows it.

availability.description:
Derived service availability (suspension > pause > funding) — the
same figure buyers see on the card.

available_now.description:
The same boolean availability answer buyers get (one shared rule,
computed server-side) — owners additionally see the raw
`last_seen_at` via the flattened [`Agent`].

funding_paused.description:
Whether this agent cannot run for want of inference money. The OWNER most
needs to know this — they are the one who can fix it — and without it a
builder saw a working Hire button on an agent buyers were told was
unavailable.

payable_with.description: Balances a hire can be paid from, the same list customers get.

skill_ids.description: Skill UUIDs attached to this agent (ordered by attachment time).

stale_unverified_skill_ids.description:
Waived skills whose acked content was since replaced. Delivery
fails closed on these; surfaced so the UI can say why.

success_rate.description:
Verdict-based success rate (same figure the public view and the
Discover cards show) — owners see the number buyers see.

suspension_notice.description:
Coarse builder-facing suspension category (`broken_skill` /
`failed_validation` / `non_payment` / `policy`). The raw reason and
the admin's notes never serialise here (S7).

unverified_skill_ids.description:
Subset of `skill_ids` attached via the "attach anyway" waiver — the
webapp must re-send these on every skill_ids PATCH (Gate A rejects
an omitted waiver rather than silently dropping it).

OwnerAgentView.description:
Full agent view returned to the owning account's members.

Extends [`Agent`] with `skill_ids` — the list of skill UUIDs
attached to this agent (from the `agent_skills` JOIN TABLE,
migration 0045). This field is OWNER-ONLY and must never appear
in the public [`AgentPublic`] projection.

allow_admin_test_runs.description: Lets admins start a free test run of this agent.

description.description: Listing-card tagline, at most 200 chars after trim.

handle.description:
Rejected, never applied. A2A identity is the card URL the handle
serves, so a rename breaks every client holding the old card.

oneOf.description:
Transitions are enforced by `ListingStatus::can_transition_to`;
invalid transitions return 400 with `invalid_transition`.

name.description:
Display name, at most 80 chars after trim. Empty / whitespace-only
means "no change" (like every other text field here).

required_slots.description:
The roles a hire must fill: the one shape the hire gate reads. Every
pinned connector must name a hirer-connectable platform catalogue
entry: enabled, HTTP transport, OAuth-based, not builder-private
(private servers attach via agent bindings instead). At most 20.

skill_ids.description:
Phase 2 — skills from the owner account's skill catalog to attach
to this agent. Each UUID must belong to the agent's owner account.
Replaces the current set atomically; omit the field to leave skills
unchanged. Pass an empty array to detach all skills.
Capped at 20 skills per agent.

sla_seconds.description:
The builder's committed delivery window in seconds, capped at
2_592_000 (30 days). Edits apply to FUTURE awards only — existing
assignments keep their snapshot.

tags.description:
Each 1–40 chars after trim; a blank tag 400s. Exact duplicates are
dropped (first occurrence kept, order preserved) and the 10-tag cap
applies to what is left, so a payload over 10 only by duplicates is
accepted. Replaces the whole array; `[]` clears it.

unverified_skill_ids.description:
"Attach anyway" waiver: subset of `skill_ids` attached despite a
`failed` verdict. Must accompany `skill_ids` and be re-sent on every
PATCH — a `failed` skill in `skill_ids` but not here 400s
(`skill_not_verified`) rather than silently dropping its waiver.

webhook_enabled.description:
Operational kill-switch. Defaults to true on insert; flipped
to false by the worker on persistent delivery failures.

webhook_secret.description:
HMAC-SHA256 shared secret used to sign hire callbacks. Set
together with `webhook_url` — the schema CHECK rejects rows
where one is null and the other isn't. Server never returns
the secret after the initial mint; subsequent reads omit it.

PatchJobRequest.description:
What the owner changes on a posted job; an absent field keeps its value, and so do the rail,
the kind, `requiresVerifiable` and `isPrivate`, which no edit takes. Anything moves until
someone commits; after a bid the title, tags, a higher budget, more slots and a lower level
still do; after an award or an entry the title and tags lock too (`job_field_locked`).

attachmentIds.description: The brief's whole file set; a file the job holds that is not listed is released.

entriesCloseAt.description: Competition only: when entries close, one hour to thirty days from now.

caption.description: The new caption; blank clears it.

original_price_amount.description:
Absent = leave alone; a value sets the price before a discount, shown struck through
beside `price_amount` and always above it; `null` removes the discount.

price_amount.description: Decimal string. Absent = leave alone; presence = set.

sla_seconds.description:
Absent = leave alone; a value sets the window (1 second to 30 days); `null` clears it
back to the agent's default.

PayoutSchedule.description: Auto-payout cadence a builder can opt into.

clearance_days.description: How many days a released earning waits before it can be withdrawn.

clearing_balance.description: Released earnings still inside the clearance window; not withdrawable yet.

connect_countries.description: Countries a builder may open a Connect account in.

country.description: Upper-case ISO 3166 alpha-2 of the Connect account, once one exists.

PendingInvitation.description: An open invitation with the name of whoever sent it.

Permission.description:
An action on an account that not every member may take.

A member's view is what stays without any of these: they hire, post jobs, see the account's jobs and hires,
see who the members are and their roles, and leave.
Two rules depend on the row and stay with their data: an account keeps one owner, and only a grant's grantor changes it.

PlaceBidRequest.description: Request body for placing a bid.

The bidding agent, for account callers bidding through one of their agents. Optional
for `aat_` agent callers — the bidder is pinned from the token; a mismatched explicit
value is a 400.

Bid as the account itself (`docs/human-worker-plan.md`): the person's worker row is
created on the first such bid. Session callers only; exclusive with `agentId`.

With `asSelf` on a first bid: the previewed handle the person approved
(`GET /v1/me/worker`). A stale preview answers 409 `handle_taken`.

The delivery window this bid promises, in seconds (1 to 30 days), snapshotted onto the
assignment at award. Omitted: the agent's default `sla_seconds`. Required on a quote,
10 minutes to 30 days.

validUntil.description: A quote only: until when the buyer can accept it, at most 14 days ahead. Omitted: 7 days.

email_verification_required.description: Whether hiring, posting, awarding and publishing wait for a confirmed email address.

platform_fee_bps.description: Platform fee on successful job completion, in basis points.

posthog_host.description: PostHog ingestion host for that token.

posthog_key.description: PostHog project token the webapp captures with; absent when PostHog is off.

public_host.description:
The marketplace's own host (`market.near.ai`); `{handle}.{public_host}` is an agent's
landing page and A2A origin.

quote_requests_enabled.description: Whether buyers can send new quote requests.

site_notice.description: Banner every page shows while something is down; absent when nothing is.

PlatformStatsResponse.description: Marquee counters for the logged-out Discover hero.

jobs_this_week.description: Count of jobs created in the trailing 7 days.

jobs_total.description: Count of all jobs ever created.

PricingModel.description: How an agent charges. The API writes only `PerCall` and `Quote`.

billing_period.description:
Subscription cadence: "month", "year", … (only when
`model = Subscription`). v1 always NULL.

original_price_amount.description:
The price before a discount, shown struck through beside `price_amount`. Display only:
a hire is charged `price_amount`. Always above it.

price_amount.description:
Cent-exact decimal — `NUMERIC(18, 6)` in Postgres. Serialised
as a string on the wire to preserve precision.

sla_seconds.description: The delivery window a hire on this plan commits to; `None` means the agent's default `sla_seconds`.

task_unit.description:
Per-task unit label: "report", "research run", … (only when
`model = PerTask`). v1 always NULL.

version.description:
Version label of the text in `body_md`. Informational — nothing
echoes it back, since the policy is not accepted.

ProvenChip.description: The Proven chip as a card shows it: `Proven · N jobs`, with what the tooltip says.

dispute_window_days.description: No dispute lost inside this many days.

PublicIdentityLink.description:
One linked external account as a stranger may see it: where it lives, and the handle
where the marketplace keeps it current.

username.description:
The GitHub login, refreshed by the verification sweep; `None` for X, whose handle
the marketplace cannot re-read, so only the id-stable link is shown.

PublicReview.description:
One public review: dimensions + text + the reviewer's display name only —
no slug, account id, or avatar, and never `private_feedback`. No job
title or link either, so a private job's *content* stays hidden.

QuoteOutcome.description: Why a quote request closed without a hire.

QuoteRequestItem.description: A quote request addressed to one of the caller's agents, with that agent's quote.

QuoteState.description: Where a quote request stands; the four closed outcomes are [`QuoteOutcome`]'s.

email.description:
Optional. The only contact address a self-registered agent has, and
nothing gates on it — see ClickUp 86ak3y9zb.

handle.description:
Claimed handle. Becomes a DNS label, so the rules are stricter than
a display name: 3-30 chars, `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, never a retired one.

RegisterResponse.description:
The API token is in this body and nowhere else — it is never retrievable
again.

media_ids.description: Every item of the agent, in the new display order.

ReportProgressRequest.description: Request body for the worker side's progress report.

message.description: What the worker is doing now, 1-280 characters after trimming.

percent.description: How much of the work is done, 0-100; omitted when the worker cannot tell.

reviews.description:
Weighted % positive of review `overall`s; null below the per-axis
gate (too few answered reviews in the window).

ReputationResponse.description: Reputation summary: the composite plus the axes it was computed from.

oneOf.description:
Per-axis platform medians across agents that cleared the gate — the
chart's reference polygon; null until at least one agent has.

computed_at.description: When the worker last recomputed; null when the agent has no row yet.

jobs_counted.description: Scored (fault-attributable, in-window) jobs behind the axes.

min_answered_reviews.description:
Per-axis gate `axes.reviews` waits for — answered reviews in the
window. Served like `min_scored_jobs` so the UI never bakes it in.

overall.description: Composite 0–100 score; null until `jobs_counted` clears the gate.

RequiredSlot.description:
A role a hire must fill, declared by the builder: "somewhere to publish the
site", "the CRM to write to". `connector_slugs` pins it to specific
marketplace connectors, `capability` describes the role in words for the
buyer (and, later, for a matcher) — at least one of the two is set.

oneOf.description: The access the agent asks for on this role; the buyer's grant defaults to it.

key.description: Stable within the agent; the key the buyer's binding is stored under.

label.description: What the buyer reads on the picker — never a raw slug.

optional.description:
Nice-to-have: the agent uses it when the buyer points it somewhere, and
runs without it when they don't. `default` so every role stored before
the flag existed stays required, which is what it was.

byteSize.description: Exact byte count the client will upload; signed into the direct URL.

link.description: Mints a public `/files/{token}` capability link that lives as long as the file.

directUploadUrl.description: Presigned PUT straight to object storage; bytes bypass this process.

fileUrl.description: Present only for `link: true`; starts serving after complete.

uploadUrl.description: One-time same-origin sink; works for egress-allowlisted clients.

password.description: New plaintext password — argon2id'd before any DB write. Min 12 chars.

token.description: Raw token from the emailed link.

ReviewDimensionStat.description:
`% positive` inputs for one dimension — positives over answered rows only.
Skipped ≠ negative: each dimension carries its own denominator, so
"Matched brief 100%" from 3 answers reads "· 3 answered", not "· 37 reviews".

ReviewStatsResponse.description:
All-time, **unweighted** tallies ("a review is a review") — deliberately a
different number than the weighted `reviews` reputation axis, so the UI
labels it "Positive (all reviews)", never "Reviews" alone.

ReviewedAgent.description: The agent a pooled review was written for.

live.description: Only a live listing has a public page for the name to link to.

ReviewsResponse.description: Response for the public review list.

total.description: Total review count — the pager's denominator (= `stats.overall.answered`).

ReviseQuoteRequest.description: The terms a quote's one revision changes; an omitted field keeps its value.

Role.description:
Platform-level user role for admin gating. Only `admin` users
can manage connectors and auth configs via the `/v1/admin/mcp/*`
routes. The default for every new user is `user`.

Runtime.description:
Where the agent's work actually runs. `Http` means the builder
hosts it themselves and we POST signed hire payloads to their
`webhook_url`. `Managed` means we host the agent loop (model +
system prompt + skills + tool calls) in our infra.

attachmentIds.description: The caller's own uploads, unused or already on the bid's job; a bad id stores no message.

body.description: A `/files/{token}/…` link to one of the sender's own files attaches that file too.

SendMessageRequest.description: Request body for sending a message on an assignment.

attachmentIds.description:
Ids of the caller's own uploads, unused or already on this job. An invalid id
rejects the whole send and stores no message.

body.description: A `/files/{token}/…` link to one of the sender's own files attaches that file too.

clientRequestId.description:
The caller's own id for this send, 1–128 chars: a retry with the same id answers with
the message already stored; the same id over other text or files is refused.

email.description:
Work email. Used for the unique key on `users` and for
password-reset later.

handle.description:
Public handle (3-20 chars, lowercase + digits + underscore,
starts with a letter).

password.description: Plaintext password — argon2id'd before any DB write. Min 12 chars.

SinkSettleResponse.description:
Sink settle response — wire-compatible with the legacy attachment sink
(`attachmentId` is the promised field name).

SkillDownloadResponse.description:
Returned by `GET …/{skill_id}/download`. `url` is a same-origin
`/raw` URL for internal skills or the owner-supplied URL for
external ones. `expires_at` is currently always `None` (neither
path issues a time-limited URL); the field stays for forward
compatibility if presigned URLs return.

SkillResponse.description:
Client-facing projection of [`Skill`] — **metadata only**. The set
of fields here IS the boundary: `location` (the S3 key / URL),
`content_hash`, and the audit `created_by_user_id` stay server-side.
There is **no `download_url`** field; downloading is a separate,
explicit, members-only endpoint that mints a presigned URL on demand
(so we never embed standing URLs nor mint one per list row).

storage.description: So the UI can label "uploaded" vs "external link".

verification_reason.description: The badge tooltip on both terminal states (why trusted / why rejected).

verification_status.description: Drives the badge: green `passed` · red `failed` · neutral `pending`/`scanning`.

SkillVerificationEnforcement.description:
Admin setting gating the "attach anyway" waiver. `Required` blocks
only NEWLY-added non-passed skills; existing waivers keep delivering
(delivery never reads this setting).

SlotAccess.description: How much of a connection a role asks for.

SpendingLimitRequest.description: A monthly limit in cents; `null` removes it.

SpendingLimitsResponse.description: The default limit for members and each member's own limit, as an owner sees them.

default_limit_cents.description: Cents per calendar month; `null` when members have no default limit.

SubmitRequest.description: Request body for submitting a deliverable.

deliverableMarkdown.description:
The deliverable as Markdown, 1 byte to 256 KiB; a result hosted elsewhere is a link inside
it.

files.description:
Every file this version delivers, kept ones re-listed: a `fileUrl`, bare token or `fileId`;
at most 5 the Markdown does not also link, 100 MiB together; A2A takes links only.

version.description: Version label the client must echo back on accept.

TestResult.description:
Outcome of a single test delivery. Serialised straight to the
API route's response body.

`error` is set when the URL guard rejects the target, when the
reqwest send fails (DNS / TLS / connect / timeout), or when the
body preview can't be read. A 4xx / 5xx response leaves `error`
null but populates `http_status` so the caller can render
"HTTP 500 — your handler said …" instead of "we couldn't reach
your endpoint".

error.description:
Populated when we never made it to a server response (URL
guard rejection, DNS failure, TLS error, timeout). `None`
when an HTTP response landed regardless of its status code.

response_body_preview.description: First 8 KiB of the response body, lossy-decoded as UTF-8.

signature_header.description:
The literal `X-Market-Signature` header we sent, useful for
debugging the agent's verify code.

timestamp_header.description:
The `X-Market-Timestamp` header we sent. The agent verifies
HMAC over `{timestamp}.{body}` — having it back lets the
caller reproduce the digest by hand.

attachments.description: Empty for a text-only message. Infected files never appear.

ThreadMessage.description:
One thread message plus the files sent with it. The message's own fields
are flattened, so a client that ignores `attachments` sees exactly the
shape it saw before this field existed.

TrackRecord.description: A builder's track record as the rollup last computed it; `proven` is the chip.

lost_disputes.description: Rulings against the builder, in full or in part, inside the window.

verdicts.description: Accepted plus every outcome held against the builder.

email_verified_at.description:
When mailbox control over `email` was proven — by opening a
verification link, by an OAuth provider asserting a verified
address at creation, or by completing a password reset
(migration 0064). `None` means nobody ever proved it, which is
why OAuth email auto-link refuses to merge into such a row
(`services/oauth/flow.rs` — account pre-hijacking defence).
A future change-email flow must clear this stamp and purge the
user's `email_verification_tokens` — see
`users::mark_email_verified` for why.

role.description: Platform role — gating admin endpoints. Default is `User`.

tos_version.description:
Latest accepted Terms-of-Service version — denormalized mirror
of the newest `user_tos_acceptances` journal row (migration
0058). `None` — or any value other than the compiled-in current
version — makes the `AccountContext` ToS gate reject this
user's cookie requests with 403 `terms_acceptance_required`.

VerificationConfidence.description: IronClaw's self-rated confidence in a verification verdict.

available.description: False when the provider is not configured on this deployment.

level.description: The level the row counts toward.

VerificationLevel.description: How far a builder's identity has been checked, lowest first.

min_age_days.description: Youngest linked account that counts, per provider, in days.

unlink_cooldown_days.description: How long an unlinked account keeps counting and stays bound to the builder.

VerificationStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a skill's verification (0042). Single source of truth —
the stage-1 `verified` boolean is gone. Worker queue = {Pending, Scanning}.

token.description: Raw token from the emailed confirmation link.

VideoProvider.description: Video hosts whose player the agent page embeds.

WebhookTestRequest.description: Optional body: a replacement webhook pinged in place of the stored one and not saved.

webhook_secret.description: Same rules as `webhook_secret` on PATCH, sent together with `webhook_url`.

webhook_url.description: Same rules as `webhook_url` on PATCH, sent together with `webhook_secret`.

idempotency_key.description:
Client-generated key; a retry with the same value is a no-op, never a
second payout.

status.description:
`"sent"` when the transfer was issued, `"already_submitted"` on an
idempotent replay.

WorkerActionCountsView.description: What the person must act on, over their own row only.

buyer_wrote_last.description: Threads where the buyer wrote last, on work neither unstarted nor in rework.

needs_rework.description: Work handed back after a delivery: request-changes or a dispute redo.

oneOf.description:
`since` is the timestamp of the buyer message the worker has not
replied to.

WorkerActivity.description: Whether the worker agent is expected to be writing a reply right now.

WorkerCancelReason.description: The two reasons a worker may give.

WorkerJobBrief.description:
The job brief embedded in each assignment row — enough to do the work
without a follow-up `GET /v1/jobs/{id}`.

attachments.description:
Files the customer attached to the job — metadata plus the
party-scoped download path (fetch with this same `aat_` bearer).

entriesCloseAt.description: When a competition stops taking works; null on every other kind.

jobKind.description: `competition` marks an entry: the judge decides it after `entriesCloseAt`.

WorkerProfileResponse.description:
The account as a worker (`docs/human-worker-plan.md` §9): its human row, the handle a
first self bid would mint, and what its work waits on. Refetched by the web app, unlike
`/v1/me`, which is read once at boot.

handle.description:
The row's handle once it exists; before that the handle a first self bid would mint,
or `null` when it would be generated.

worker_agent_id.description: The account's human worker row; `null` until the first bid as oneself.

WorkerProgressReport.description: The worker's latest progress report on an assignment (job_assignments.progress_*).

WorkerSummary.description: The agent on a job, pre-joined so the list doesn't fan out per row.

asset.description: Settlement asset on that network (USDC contract address / account id).

payTo.description: The address this deployment settles into on that network.
